output.methodChoice: Collected X4 (independent calibration site visit) and X13 (quality-lab teardown, retest and claim breakdown); no other items read.
output.brief:
What is going on: the rise in VA-220 failures is most likely caused by defective Pellacott valves built in 2026. Their slide seals are deforming and unseating, which leaks at the seat. Installer firms and firmware 4.2 do not explain it: failure rates are similar across legacy and new installers and across firmware versions, while Durrant-Hale valves stay low throughout. Pellacott's SupplierPath score rose because its test certificates became complete, but the independent calibration visit found rig LT-04 out of service since January, no VA-220 test program on the other rigs, and certificate tables that repeat a few sequences going back to 2025. The leak tests on those certificates probably were not performed.

How sure: fairly sure about the defect and the bad records. The seal change is the likely cause but is not yet proven, because the seal compound was not analysed and it is confounded with the move to Line 3.

Next steps: quarantine all 2026-built Pellacott VA-220 stock, including the six held lots, and suspend its dock-to-stock status. Do not release the held lots on Pellacott's new certificates. Release only after Brenmoor-run helium testing. Do not charge installers. Have the seal compound analysed, and change SupplierPath to credit only verified test records.
